                               BLUFFDALE CITY PLANNING COMMISSION
                                        MEETING AGENDA
                                   Wednesday, December 7, 2022


Notice is hereby given that the Bluffdale City Planning Commission will hold a public meeting on
Wednesday, December 7, 2022, at 6:00 p.m., or as soon thereafter as possible at the Bluffdale City Hall,
2222 West 14400 South, Bluffdale, Utah. This meeting may also be broadcast live to the public on the City’s
website www.bluffdale.com. Notice is further given that access to this meeting by Commission members
may be by electronic means via telephone conference call.

PLANNING COMMISSION BUSINESS MEETING 6:00 PM
   1. Roll Call.
   2. Invocation/Thought/Reading and Pledge of Allegiance.
   3. Approval of the Planning Commission meeting minutes from November 2, 2022.

ADMINISTRATIVE ITEMS:

   4. CONSIDERATION AND VOTE on a Plat Amendment Application for Kenna Lane Subdivision Lot 104
      Amended in the R-1-43 Zone located at approximately 14230 South 3600 West, Jessie Iacono,
      Applicant (Application 2022-52) - Staff Presenter, Ellen Oakman.

   5. CONSIDERATION AND VOTE on a Plat Amendment for Saddleback III Commercial Condominiums
      amending Lot 3 Reagan Cove Subdivision for 7.96 acres to create 30 commercial units and common
      areas located at approximately 13927 South 2700 West Howland Partners, Applicant (Application
      2022-12) - Staff Presenter, Jennifer Robison.

   6. PUBLIC HEARING, CONSIDERATION AND VOTE on a Preliminary Subdivision Application for
      Banner Hill Plat B for 62 residential townhome units including private streets and common areas in
      the Mixed-Use Zone (MU) located at approximately 15200 South Porter Rockwell Boulevard, Banner
      Hill LLC, Applicants (Application 2021-40) - Staff Presenter, Jennifer Robison.

   7. CONSIDERATION AND VOTE on a Site Plan Application for Banner Hill Plat B for 62 residential
      townhome units including private streets and common areas in the Mixed-Use Zone (MU) located
      at approximately 15200 South Porter Rockwell Boulevard, Banner Hill LLC, Applicants (Application
      2021-40) - Staff Presenter, Jennifer Robison.

   8. PUBLIC HEARING, CONSIDERATION AND VOTE on a Preliminary Subdivision Application for
      Bluffdale Highlands including 7.53 acres to create seven lots in the R-1-43 Residential Zone located
      at approximately 14870 South Redwood Road, Mark Greenwood, Applicant (Application 2022-32) –
      Staff Presenter, Ellen Oakman.
LEGISLATIVE ITEMS:

   9. PUBLIC HEARING, CONSIDERATION AND RECOMMENDATION on proposed amendments to the
      Bluffdale City Land Use Ordinance, Title 11, Chapter 11, Special Purpose and Overlay Zones, to
      create a new zoning ordinance chapter and map designation for The Bluff at Point Crossing Special
      Development Zone (SD-X) for 19.47 acres including, but not limited to; commercial and residential
      uses, open space and trails, public and private streets, and specific site and architectural design

19   1.       Roll Call.
20
21   All members of the Planning Commission were present with the exception of Debbie Cragun and

23
24   2.       Invocation/Thought/Reading and Pledge of Allegiance.
25
26   Ulises Flynn offered the invocation and led the Pledge of Allegiance.
27
28   3.       Approval of the Planning Commission Meeting Minutes from October 19, 2022.
29
30   Kory Luker moved to APPROVE the minutes from the October 19, 2022, meeting of the
31   Planning Commission. Ulises Flynn seconded the motion. Vote on motion: Ulises Flynn-Aye;
32   Erik Swanson-Aye; Johnny Loumis, Jr.-Aye; Kory Luker-Aye.                  The motion passed
33   unanimously.
34
35   4.       Planning Commissioners HB-409 Training – Staff Presenter, Grant Crowell, Zoning
36            Administrator.
37
38   City Planner/Economic Development Director, Grant Crowell, provided the training.        He first
39   addressed parking, which he stated can be a very complex issue. The consensus of the Planning
40   Commission was for Mr. Crowell to address residential and suburban parking. Mr. Crowell explained

                                                      1
                             DRAFT – FOR DISCUSSION PURPOSES ONLY

                             BLUFFDALE CITY PLANNING COMMISSION
                                      MEETING MINUTES
                                   Wednesday, November 2, 2022

 1   that any time he goes to a professional conference, the issue of parking is invariably discussed because
 2   it is a thoroughly researched topic.
 3
 4   Parking requirements begin with categorizing the proposed project since the category of the project
 5   will dictate the parking requirements. For example, for a church, the requirement is one stall per 100
 6   square feet of the building. If it is a hospital, it must be one space per 200 square feet. A medical
 7   office would be different. Engineers are not parking analysts, so more detailed information needs to
 8   be provided to Staff so that they can determine what the required parking will be. Sometimes, a
 9   multiple-use development creates unknowns because only time will tell how the space will be used
10   and how that use will impact the parking requirements. The last building in a multiple-building
11   business park might pose challenges to parking when an owner applies for a Business License.
12
13   Commissioner Swanson brought up discussions that took place with The Centrum. It was noted that
14   the City’s parking requirements were quite high but they were willing to meet that requirement. Mr.
15   Crowell explained that since there is still no public transit service in Bluffdale, there are impacts on
16   parking. In homes where there are garages, families are typically large, so the garage becomes a
17   storage area rather than a parking area. Thus, residential parking spills onto the street, thereby
18   creating the need to require more parking spaces.
19
20   In areas where there are apartment complexes, developers tend to have longitudinal data that indicates
21   that the parking requirement should be 1.7 to 1.8 parking stalls per apartment. The City's minimum
22   is two parking stalls per apartment despite what developers suggest. The neighboring residents
23   believe that the requirement should be even higher to mitigate parking issues in their neighborhood.
24   Mr. Crowell acknowledged that the best efforts by the City will still not eliminate the challenges that
25   will occur on Rising Star Way.
26
27   Mr. Crowell reviewed the history of Independence, which dates back to before 2010. A new version
28   was developed in 2012 and even more, changes took place in 2014 that led to the creation of The
29   Market Place and Beacon Hills. The requirement was two spaces per residence but there was not
30   much discussion about guest parking. The problems associated with guest parking resulted in
31   research in 2016 by Senior City Planner, Jennifer Robison that focused on parking at Independence

                                                         2
                            DRAFT – FOR DISCUSSION PURPOSES ONLY

                            BLUFFDALE CITY PLANNING COMMISSION
                                     MEETING MINUTES
                                  Wednesday, November 2, 2022

 1   at the Point. The discussions included the needed size of driveways so that sidewalks are not blocked.
 2   Also, the number of bedrooms in a residence was factored into the parking requirement. The City
 3   Council also realized that alleys are not a particularly favored option as part of the housing product
 4   mix.
 5
 6   Some parts of Bluffdale have a very complex mixture of residential types. Some of the initial
 7   assumptions that were made proved to be inaccurate because people will do what they want to,
 8   regardless of what the planners anticipated.       Mr. Crowell explained that some of the later
 9   developments, such as Cobalt Village, have generated fewer complaints about parking because of the
10   enhanced parking requirements that were adopted. Different cities take different approaches than
11   Bluffdale does.
12
13   Currently, for single-family dwellings, Bluffdale requires two parking spaces per dwelling unit. That
14   includes the requirement for a two-car garage with a 20-foot driveway. Shared driveways are not
15   common but the guest parking for such residences is one guest parking stall per three dwelling units.
16   The public street cannot be counted toward the parking requirement as was allowed previously. For
17   multi-family dwelling units, the parking requirement is two per dwelling unit. If it is a townhome
18   with a 20-foot driveway, the guest parking requirement is one space per four dwelling units. Multi-
19   family townhomes without a driveway require one guest parking space per three units and two spaces
20   in a garage. For apartment buildings, the parking requirement is two spaces for one or two-bedroom
21   units and 2.5 spaces for three or more bedrooms. He reported that some communities have eliminated
22   all parking requirements because the market should decide. The reason for that lack of requirement
23   was unknown. One complaint that is sometimes expressed is the fact that someone has parked on a
24   public street in front of a person’s house that is ostensibly “reserved” for the homeowner. The bottom
25   line is that there will always be parking complaints. The more parking that is provided, the more
26   parking demand there will be, and someone will have a parking problem and become disgruntled.
27
28   Commissioner Loumis could foresee something happening at Porter Rockwell Boulevard and I-15
29   when the prison property develops. He urged the City to keep an eye on that area to see how it is
30   developed and what kinds of provisions are made for pedestrian crossings and parking. Mr. Crowell
31   stated that the Executive Director for The Point will be present at the City Council’s Work Session
                                                       3
                             DRAFT – FOR DISCUSSION PURPOSES ONLY

                             BLUFFDALE CITY PLANNING COMMISSION
                                      MEETING MINUTES
                                   Wednesday, November 2, 2022

 1   on November 9 to provide an update. The overarching concept is that it will be a “15-minute city,”
 2   which means that there will be so many things available in that small area that a person could get to
 3   anything within a 15-minute walk. Mr. Crowell liked the concept but was curious to see how
 4   economically feasible the concept will be and how it will negatively impact Bluffdale. Bluffdale does
 5   not have a duration ordinance for parking, except for winter parking when there is a snowstorm. In
 6   instances where a person is using the street as a long-term parking site, evidence could be gathered to
 7   determine if the parking is associated with running a business, if the individual has a Business License
 8   to run that business, and if the parking falls within the terms of the license. Mr. Crowell explained
 9   that unattached trailers and unlicensed vehicles pose a different set of challenges that could be
10   addressed.
11
12   If there are situations that present a safety hazard, the City Engineer should be consulted to determine
13   whether there is empirical data that would warrant corrective action, including red-curbing a portion
14   of a street. It is important to make decisions based on empirical data and not on ad hoc anecdotal
15   information.
16
17   Mr. Crowell briefly reviewed the types of roads the City has classified, such as:
18      ▪   Arterial to freeway;
19      ▪   Smaller arterial, such as 14600 South;
20      ▪   Major collector; and
21      ▪   Minor collector.
22   Local residential streets include:
23      ▪   Street cross-sections that have curb, gutter, and sidewalk, which are generally 30 feet from
24          back-to-back of curb. Parking occurs in many variations and includes complex engineering
25          analyses.
26
27   Mr. Crowell stated that Staff would conduct some traffic training and traffic study training.
28
29   In response to Commissioner Loumis’ question regarding the current Utah Department of
30   Transportation (“UDOT”) plans for the intersection of Porter Rockwell Boulevard and 14600 South,
31   Mr. Crowell reported he recently visited with a UDOT Consultant to perform an analysis to determine


                                                        4
                             DRAFT – FOR DISCUSSION PURPOSES ONLY

                             BLUFFDALE CITY PLANNING COMMISSION
                                      MEETING MINUTES
                                   Wednesday, November 2, 2022

 1   what that intersection should look like. There was discussion that the intersection might need to be
 2   grade separated because of the anticipated traffic that could go through, especially as The Point is
 3   developed on the former prison site. It might even include triple-turn lanes. Mr. Crowell clarified
 4   that he still did not truly know the answer to that question and stated that several changes will take
 5   place.
 6
 7   In response to Commissioner Flynn’s question about available recourses when snow removal does
 8   not take place as it needs to, Mr. Crowell explained that police response will be difficult because they
 9   are busy responding to accidents. The Code Enforcement Officer is not allowed, by State law, to
10   write tickets to code violators.
11
12   Mr. Crowell reported one Planning Commission Meeting was scheduled for December but there
13   likely will not be training. The minimum requirement will be attendance at the meeting to meet the
14   HB-409 training requirement.

                                                 STAFF REPORT
                                                2 December 2022


To:          City of Bluffdale Planning Commission
Prepared By: Jennifer Robison, Senior Planner, on behalf of the DRC

Re:     Saddleback III Commercial Condominiums - Plat Amendment Application
        Application No:      2022-12
        Applicant(s):        Howland Partners
        Address:             13927 South 2700 West
        Zoning:              General Commercial
        Acreage:             7.96 acres
        Request:             To approve the plat amendment to create 30 commercial units and
                             common areas on Lot 3 of the original Reagan Cove Subdivision.

SUMMARY
The applicants are proposing to create 30 commercial units for individual ownership as phase 3 of the
overall Saddleback at the Point project. The original preliminary plat was for 3 lots including the adjacent
property for the Reagan Cove residential project and was approved by the Planning Commission on
September 29, 2021. Since the preliminary plat approval, the Reagan Cove Final Plat has received staff
approval and is in process of being reviewed for recording.

Adequate Public Facilities and Infrastructure. All necessary public facilities exist or will be installed with the
construction for this plat amendment.

DRC REVIEW AND COMMENTS
On behalf of the City Manager, the City’s staff involved in development review and meets together as a
Development Review Committee (DRC). The DRC generally consists of the City Manager, City Attorney, City
Engineer, Public Works Director, the City Planner, and other outside consultants as needed from time to
time. The comments of the DRC members have been included in this staff report and the recommended
conditions of approval for the project.

City Engineer. The outstanding requirements by the City Engineer and Public Works Department are
included in the recommended conditions of approval. The layout, design and construction of all
subdivisions are subject to the Bluffdale City Engineering Standards and Specifications.

Fire Marshal. There are no outstanding requirements from the Fire Marshal.

City Planner. The Planning Division is recommending approval with compliance to all City land use
ordinances and with the recommended conditions.

                                               STAFF REPORT
                                              2 December 2022

To:          City of Bluffdale Planning Commission
Prepared By: Jennifer Robison, Senior Planner, on behalf of the DRC

Re: Banner Hill Plat B (West) – Preliminary Subdivision Plat and Site Plan Applications
       Application No:           2021-40
       Applicant(s):             Banner Hill, LLC
       Project Location:         Approximately 15200 South Porter Rockwell Boulevard
       General Plan:             Mixed Use
       Zoning:                   MU-Mixed Use (as modified by the Independence at the Point Development
                                 Agreement)
       Acreage:                   8.55 acres
       Request:                  Approval of proposed Preliminary Subdivision Plat for Banner Hill Plat B for
                                 62 townhome units with associated private streets, common areas and
                                 open space within Independence at the Point project.


SUMMARY
Subject to the DRC staff’s recommendations, the proposed applications meet the City requirements for
Preliminary Plat approval as outlined in the Bluffdale City Subdivision Ordinance, the Mixed-Use zoning
district ordinance, and the contractual requirements of the Independence at the Point Development
Agreement (DA).

Background. The Comprehensive Land Use Master Plan exhibit in the Independence at the Point Project
Plan (PP) identifies the area planned for the Banner Hill (West) townhome project as area P2 allowing 245
residential units. The PP also provides other land use standards for residential development.

ANALYSIS
Anticipated Uses, Layout and Access. All units are accessed from a 33 feet wide private street on Insignia
Lane and a 26 feet wide private street on Emblem Lane and Brotherhood Way. All streets are accessed
from two connections to Heritagecrest Way which is a public street and connects to Harmon Day Drive to
the north. A temporary second access is provided with a 20 feet wide easement with the adjacent property
owner, Geneva Rock Products. The future dedication and construction of the permanent public street
connection to Porter Rockwell Boulevard will be provided with development of the Geneva parcel. All
private streets will be owned and maintained by a homeowner’s association (HOA).

This plat is showing locations of buildings, but not creating individual townhome units as a typical


                                         Preliminary Subdivision Plat and Site Plan Applications –Banner Hill Plat B (West)
                                                                        December 2, 2022, Planning Commission Meeting
                                                                                                                    Page 1
development. The owners intend to maintain ownership of all units in the project which does not require
the units to be created as individually separate units. This project is intended to be for rent and not for
individual ownership of tenants. If the owners choose at a future date to terminate their singular
ownership of the project, this will necessitate a plat amendment to create individual units.

The units along Insignia Drive will be 30 typical townhome units with or without a driveway. The rest of the
32 units will be a new stacked unit design with a 20 feet long driveway to provide options for parking. The
parking analysis is provided below.

Parking. The City Code 11-12-3 for off-street and guest parking applies to the Banner Hill West project. All
townhome units without a driveway are required to provide two (2) parking spaces within the enclosed
garage and one (1) guest parking space per three (3) dwelling units. The parking will be monitored and
enforced by the owner’s association. No parking will be allowed on Heritagecrest Way. The parking
calculation for the overall project is as follows:

           Parking Requirement:           Required Parking Stalls =           Parking Stalls Provided =

                                             30 TYPICAL UNITS
        2 parking spaces per dwelling
                                                     60                                   60
        unit enclosed in garage.
        Guest parking: 1 guest parking
        space per 3 dwelling units w/o               10                                   29
        driveway.
                                             32 STACKED UNITS
        1 parking spaces per dwelling
        unit enclosed in garage/1                    32                                   32
        space in driveway.
        Guest parking: 1 guest parking
        space per 3 dwelling units w/o               22                                   42
        driveway.

Adequate Public Facilities and Infrastructure. All adequate public facilities will be installed with the project
construction for this project.

Setbacks. The minimum setbacks for all residential units are provided in the PP. The 30 units are typical of
an alley-loaded unit because most of the units do not provide a driveway. The typical front setback is 10
feet, side setback is 3 feet, and rear setback is 3 feet. The setback from the alley/street to the building
structure is a minimum of 5 feet but may increase for various units based on the layout. All the units for the
project comply with the required setbacks.

Open Space and Trails. Although no public parks are required to be dedicated or constructed with this
project, the site does contain some private owner’s association controlled private open space. A public
trail will be constructed along Heritagecrest Way and connect to the existing trail built with the road
extension to access this property. An additional trail connection will be constructed with this project on
the north slope to provide future connections to other City properties. Due to the topography of the site,
the final designs and locations are being determined by the engineering department.

                                                                         December 2, 2022, Planning Commission Meeting
                                                                                                                     Page 2
DRC REVIEW AND COMMENTS
On behalf of the City Manager, the City’s staff involved in development review and administration meets
together as a Development Review Committee (DRC). The DRC generally consists of the City Manager, City
Attorney, City Engineer, Public Works Director, the City Planner, and other outside consultants as needed
from time to time. The comments of the DRC members have been included in this staff report and the
recommended conditions of approval for the project.

City Engineer. The outstanding requirements by the City Engineer and Public Works Department are
included in the recommended conditions of approval. The layout, design and construction of all
subdivisions are subject to the Bluffdale City Engineering Standards and Specifications.

Fire Marshal. No outstanding comments. Plat and Site Plan approved.

City Planner. The Planning Division is recommending approval with the recommended conditions.

DRC STAFF RECOMMENDATION FOR BANNER HILL PLAT B PRELIMINARY SUBDIVISION APPLICATION:

DRC Staff recommends that the Planning Commission approve Banner Hill Plat B Preliminary Subdivision
Application subject to the following conditions:

1.   That all requirements of the City Codes, adopted ordinances and the Independence at the Point
     Project Plan are met and adhered to for the applications.
2.   That the preliminary plat complies with the Bluffdale City Engineering Standards and Specifications
     and recommendations by the City Engineer and Public Works Department for all relevant
     construction and plat drawings.
3.   That all construction drawings be approved and stamped by the City Engineer prior to any
     construction of improvements.
4.   That the project adheres to all requirements of the International Fire Code.
5.   That all private open space, landscaping, parking areas and alleys/streets be owned and maintained
     by the owner’s association and improvements installed as per approved plan.
6.   No parking is permitted on Heritagcrest Way.
7.   That the applicant receives Final Subdivision Plat approval by the Land Use Authority for the project
     prior to the recordation of the Final Plat.
8.   That the applicant completes final designs with the city engineers and construct the trail connection
     on the north slope as planned.

                                                Memo
Date: November 29, 2022
From: Dan Tracer, PE, Assistant City Engineer
To:       Grant Crowell, Zoning Administrator
RE:       Bluffdale Highlands– Preliminary Plat Approval



In an effort to ensure all preliminary plat applications are compliant with City standards and
ordinances, the City Engineering Department conducts a review of all preliminary plat applications.
We have completed our review of the Bluffdale Highlands Preliminary Plat and recommend
approval be granted with the requirement that the following conditions be met prior to
construction or plat recordation:
      •   The applicant continue to revise the project Drainage Report to meet City Standards and
          Specifications.
      •   The applicant continue to revise the project drawings and drainage report through the
          Engineering Department review process, to be in accordance with City standards and
          specifications.
      •   The applicant provide approval from South Valley Sewer District for the project.
      •   The applicant dedicate the required canal water shares or water rights to the City of
          Bluffdale in the amount of 5.0 Acre-feet per irrigable acre within the project.
      •   Applicant provide a Landscape and Irrigation Plan for the project Stormwater Pond that
          meets City Standards and Specifications.
Please contact me directly with any questions or concerns you may have.




Dan Tracer, P.E. – Assistant City Engineer
City of Bluffdale

SD-X THE BLUFFS AT POINT CROSSING ZONE



11.110.140.010 INTENT AND PURPOSE

The intent of this special development zone is to provide a land use pattern for a
complementary and compatible pedestrian friendly mix of commercial and residential uses.
It is the intent of this zone to allow for flexibility and creativity in the arrangement of uses and
unique design standards. The purpose is to develop The Bluffs at Point Crossing (“SD-X BPC
Zone”), a mixed-use community consisting of up to 65,000 square feet of commercial uses
and up to 50 residential townhome units. The SD-X BPC Zone is located adjacent to Porter
Rockwell Boulevard and Heritagecrest Way which provides vehicular and pedestrian access
for the development. Design standards and site specifications in this project are created with
this chapter and shall supersede any conflicting design standards and site specifications in
any and all applicable City ordinances. Design standards not specifically included in the SD-X
BPC Zone, shall be governed by applicable provisions of the Bluffdale City Code (BCC).


11.110.140.020 LAND USE AUTHORITY FOR SITE PLAN AND SUBDIVISION APPROVAL
A site plan approval is required for all commercial and residential buildings within the SD-X
BPC Zone. All applications are subject to the development standards and design
requirements of this chapter and the Bluffdale City Codes in title 11.150 and other applicable
BCC sections and are required to be approved by the Bluffs at Point Crossing Architectural
Review Committee (BPCARC) prior to review and approval by the Land Use Authority. City of
Bluffdale staff shall be the Land Use Authority to review and approve all site plans.
The adoption of the SD-X BPC does not constitute a subdivision of the proposed property. All
future subdivisions of land within the SD-X BPC Zone are subject to all requirements of Title
12 and other applicable sections of the Bluffdale City Code and all adopted specifications and
all applications shall be reviewed and approved by the designated Land Use Authority as
stated.

amenities as shown in Figure 1 and Figure 2. Total acreage may vary as final site plans are

anticipated layout of commercial and residential uses and does not constitute final site plan
approval. Site plan approval is required for all phases of development consistent with the
Bluffdale City Code and as outlined in this title by the authorized Land Use Authority.

11.110.140.050 COMMERCIAL DEVELOPMENT AND DESIGN STANDARDS

The commercial areas of the SD-X BPC Zone consist of approximately 12.48 acres. It is
anticipated up to 65,000 square feet of commercial and retail uses will be provided
depending upon market demand and economic opportunities. Proposed commercial uses
are shown in Table 11.110.140.060. The overall project shall provide pedestrian connections
and access to community and regional trail networks through integrated site design. The site
shall also provide vehicular access and circulation for mobility within the site and visibility
along Porter Rockwell Boulevard and Heritagecrest Way.
   A. Public Open Space and Landscaping Requirements: Open space shall be included as
      a component of all site plans, and shall include the following minimum standards:
       1. Consist of a minimum of fifteen percent (15%) of the overall acreage for the entire
          project. Site specific landscaping plans will be approved with the individual site
          plan applications and shall maintain landscaping percentages in each phase of
          development.
       2. Additional features including art, clocks, water features, or other amenities are
          highly encouraged within the SD-X BPC commercial area. These areas may include
          a central prominent gathering space with a focal feature such as a statue, water
          feature, canopy, gazebo, clock tower, or other feature as approved with the site
          plan. The central features shall be proportionate to the size and scale of the
          gathering space and may include other features such as raised planters, benches,
          trees, pedestrian scale lighting, and brick pavers or stamped concrete.
       3. Any hardscaped area featuring any of the amenities listed above used for a public
          open space shall be included in the overall tabulation for the minimum open space
          or landscaping requirement and may receive credit as a replacement for irrigated
          landscape areas.
       4. A trail network shall be provided within the project to connect the commercial and
          residential areas and create connections to other public trails within the area,
          pursuant to or as shown on concept plan Figure 2. Trail locations and

       specifications are subject to the City’s standards and shall be reviewed and
       approved with specific site plan applications.
B. All landscaped areas shall be installed in accordance with the City’s standards for
   water efficiency, parking lot landscaping, trees, shrubs, ground cover requirements,
   and irrigation design.
C. Street trees shall be planted and maintained in compliance with City standards in all
   park strips and adjacent to the trail areas. Where a park strip does not exist or allow

D. Commercial Development Standards:
   The SD-XBPC Zone provides specific development standards for the overall project.
   The purpose is to provide a sense of place and unifying theme for the project by
   elevating the quality of materials, colors, and additional amenities not typically
   required for commercial development.
   1. General Standards:
       a. Public utility easements shall meet Bluffdale City Standards.
       b. No trash, used materials, unsightly or outside storage of any kind, or non-
       licensed or abandoned vehicles shall be stored in this SD-X zone.
       c. Dumpster enclosures shall be architecturally designed and screened per
       adopted standards in BCC. Locations and materials shall be approved during site
       plan review.
   2. Commercial Location Standards:
       a. Setback Requirements: Commercial buildings and necessary appurtenances
          for utility service may be located as depicted on the concept plan with no
          specific setback requirements. Drive-through lanes shall be screened and
          buffered from adjacent sidewalks and trails by at least five feet (5’) of perimeter
          landscaping which includes vertical elements. Building locations shall be
          approved during the commercial site plan review process and shall comply
          with all adopted building and fire codes, accommodate utility easements, right
          of way requirements, transportation, and access ways, and all other applicable
          provisions of the Bluffdale City Code and adopted standards.

   b. Commercial Maximum Height: A primary building or structure may not exceed
      forty-five feet (45’) in height, nor be lower than ten feet (10’) in height. All
      buildings and structures must adhere to adopted Building and Fire Codes.
   c. Screening of utilities and equipment: Shall adhere to all BCC adopted
      requirements.
   d. Distance Between Commercial Buildings: The distance between any building

      Fire Codes in place at the time of site plan approval.
3. Commercial Parking, Loading, and Access:
   a. Parking: Total required off street parking spaces shall be a minimum of five (5)
      stalls per one thousand (1,000) useable square feet for office and retail uses.
      Sufficiency of parking stall be verified during site plan review, based on a
      professional analysis and the specific proposed uses. The spaces shall be hard
      surfaced with asphalt or concrete and be accessed from a public road by a hard
      surfaced, composed of asphalt or concrete, drive approach which meets
      adopted standards. A conceptual parking plan is presented in Figure 1.
   b. Loading and Unloading Area: Loading and unloading and service entrances
      shall not occur on or adjacent to a public street. Loading docks are not allowed
      and service areas shall be screened from traffic with berming, decorative
      masonry walls, and/or landscaping, pursuant to adopted design requirements
      in the BCC.
   c. Buildings and uses designated with drive-through lanes shall verify adequate
      stacking and queuing in their traffic analysis during site plan review.
   d. Cross-access easement agreements shall be recorded with any proposed
      subdivision to accommodate free movement of vehicular and pedestrian traffic
      and to allow shared parking throughout the project.
   e. All internal roads throughout the development are planned to be private roads
      and will be owned and maintained by the owners or users as part of the SD-
      XBPC Zone.

                                               STAFF REPORT
                                              2 December 2022

To:          City of Bluffdale Planning Commission
Prepared By: Jennifer Robison, Senior Planner

Re: Zoning Text Amendment Application – Bluffdale City Code 11.160.180 for Shared Driveways
        Application No:     2022-46
        Applicant(s):       Olin VanDerWatt
        Request:            Approve a text amendment to the Bluffdale City Land Use Ordinances
                            11.160.180 (c)(2) supplementary provisions for shared driveways to allow
                            “access to a maximum of three lots or parcels”.

SUMMARY
The City Council approved the use of shared driveways and created a set of standards for the shared
driveway to be used for constrained or isolated properties back in 2004. The Bluffdale City Code 11.160.180
provides several criteria for the shared driveway to be created. This development option is limited to the R-
1-87, R-1-43, R-1-10 or A-5 Zoning Districts where larger properties have limited access to public streets. As
property owners desire to develop larger parcels of property, the shared driveway ordinance has been and
may be continued to be used to access in-fill parcels throughout the City.

ANALYSIS
The current requirement for a shared driveway states “the shared driveway shall provide access to a
maximum of two (2) lots or parcels”. The applicant is proposing to amend the text of this provision only to
allow a maximum of three (3) lots or parcels. The applicant’s representative has met with City staff to
discuss the proposed amendment to ascertain if the increase of one additional parcel or dwelling unit on a
shared driveway would have any potential negative impacts. The City staff has reviewed the proposal and
would support the amendment along with owners complying with all other requirements within the
ordinance regarding any safety concerns.

APPROVAL CRITERIA FOR THE APPLICATION
Zoning text amendments are a legislative decision of the City Council, after receiving a recommendation
from the Planning Commission. Broad discretion is given to the City’s Land Use Authorities when making
land use decisions. The Planning Commission should establish adequate findings in support of a positive
or negative outcome and forward those findings to the City Council.

DRC REVIEW AND COMMENTS
On behalf of the City Manager, the City’s staff involved in development review and administration meets
together as a Development Review Committee (DRC). The DRC generally consists of the City Manager, City
Attorney, City Engineer, Public Works Director, the City Planner, and other outside consultants as needed

                                            Olin VanDerWatt – Zoning Text Amendment Application for Shared Driveways
                                                                      December 7, 2022, Planning Commission Meeting
                                                                                                               Page 1
from time to time. The comments of the DRC members have been included in this staff report and the
recommended conditions of approval for the project.

City Engineer. The Engineering Department would support the text amendment with the other provisions
of the ordinance provided to ensure no negative impacts on safety.

Fire Marshal. No additional comments.

City Planner. The Planning Department is recommending approval with the recommended conditions of
the engineering and fire departments.

11.160.180 Shared Driveways

  A. Scope: Except as otherwise provided in the City's land use ordinances, no building
     permit shall be issued for a dwelling located on a lot or parcel accessed by a shared
     driveway other than a dedicated and improved public street or approved private right-
     of-way.
  B. Circumstances Permitting: The creation of or the issuance of a building permit for a lot
     or parcel accessed from a shared driveway may be approved by the Zoning
     Administrator under the following circumstances:
         1. There exists certain unique circumstances that directly impact the lots or
            parcels to be accessed by the shared driveway as follows:
                a. The lots or parcels are isolated from any presently existing public streets
                    and will be isolated from any future public streets; and
                b. The property is bounded by certain physical barriers that isolate the
                    proposed lots or parcels which preclude future expansion and
                    development and deny through access to public streets.
         2. For purposes of this section, physical barriers may include: existing canals with
            recorded easements and rights-of-way that prohibit public access and crossing;
            railroad rights-of-way; terrain that prevents conventional access by public
            streets; utility easements which prohibit street access and crossing; existing
            developments of improved real property contiguous to the subject property
            that prohibits extension of through public streets to or from the lots or parcels;
            existing or proposed drainage requirements which include storm drain
            channels, retention/detention ponds, or natural creek beds which prohibit
            public street access; or limited access roads which prohibit a public street
            connection.
  C. Restrictions, Limitations: The creation of or the issuance of a building permit for a lot or
     parcel accessed by a shared driveway approved by the Zoning Administrator shall
     comply with the following restrictions and limitations:
         1. Be located within a Residential R-1-87, R-1-43, R-1-10 or Agricultural A-5 Zoning
            District.
         2. The shared driveway shall provide access to a maximum of two (2) three (3) lots
            or parcels.
         3. The lot or parcel to be accessed off of the shared driveway meets all the
            standards and requirements under the City subdivision ordinance and land use
            ordinance;
         4. Required minimum yard setback requirements shall apply to all buildings
            fronting, siding or rearing on the shared driveway or private land and shall be
            measured from the boundary of any such right-of-way nearest the building.
         5. The shared driveway has a minimum recorded right-of-way width of at least
            twenty-five feet (25') and all-weather surface of at least twenty feet (20').
         6. The shared driveway shall be improved in compliance with City standards and
            specifications for the number and intensity of lots or parcels served.
7. The shared driveway shall have a turnaround as determined necessary by the
    Fire Department.
8. No parking is permitted within the shared driveway.
9. The shared driveway shall only be used to access single-family residences.
10. Each adjoining lot or parcel using the shared driveway shall have recorded
    ownership or right-of-way access to such driveway or private lane by easement
    or fee title.
11. All dwellings on the lots or parcels shall be within four hundred feet (400') of a
    fire hydrant approved by the Fire Department and access to the fire hydrant
    shall comply with the applicable Fire Codes adopted by the City.
12. The shared driveway abuts and is accessed off of a fully improved and
    dedicated public street.
13. The shared driveway is not necessary to be dedicated as a public street to
    accomplish needed and logical street connections, to provide access to
    properties that may otherwise have no access or limited access to the detriment
    of the property, or other purpose determined to be necessary and appropriate.
    (Ord. 2018-05, 3-14-2018)
